items.followUp: What is phishing? Explain two ways to protect yourself from it.

rubric.why: Award for defining cybercrime as illegal or criminal activity carried out using a computer or the internet.
rubric.description: Defines cybercrime as a crime involving the use of a computer or the internet.
rubric.how: Look for both a crime-related term and a reference to computers or the internet.

rubric.why: Award for identifying hacking and explaining it as unauthorised access.
rubric.description: Explains hacking as gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Look for hacking together with unauthorised/unauthorized access.

rubric.why: Award for identifying identity theft and explaining the theft or misuse of someone’s identity or personal information.
rubric.description: Explains identity theft as stealing personal information or using another person’s identity.
rubric.how: Look for identity theft together with stolen personal information or impersonation.

rubric.why: Award for identifying software piracy and explaining its illegal copying or distribution of software.
rubric.description: Explains software piracy as illegally copying copyrighted software.
rubric.how: Look for software piracy together with copying and an indication that it is illegal or involves copyrighted software.

modelAnswer: Cybercrime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, a network, or the internet.
Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to another person’s computer or network.
Identity theft involves stealing someone’s personal information and using it to impersonate them.
Software piracy is illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm? Give one benefit of using it before writing a program.

rubric.why: Award for describing an algorithm as an ordered sequence of instructions or steps.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm provides ordered steps or instructions for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Look for algorithm and a reference to its sequence of instructions or steps.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that an algorithm helps plan or organise the problem’s solution before programming.
rubric.description: Explains the role of an algorithm in planning or organising a solution to a problem.
rubric.how: Look for a link between the algorithm and planning, organising, or solving the problem.

modelAnswer: An algorithm gives an ordered sequence of instructions for solving a problem.
It helps the programmer plan and organise the logic of the solution before writing the program.

items.followUp: Name two common flowchart symbols and state what each represents.

rubric.why: Award for stating that a flowchart uses standard symbols to represent its steps or operations.
rubric.description: States that standard flowchart symbols represent the steps or operations of a process.
rubric.how: Look for standard flowchart symbols and what they represent.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that arrows connect the symbols and show the process flow.
rubric.description: States that arrows connect symbols and indicate the direction or sequence of the process.
rubric.how: Look for arrows and their connecting or sequencing function.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is constructed by representing each step with the appropriate standard symbol, such as a start/end, process, or decision symbol.
The symbols are connected with arrows to show the direction and sequence of the steps.
